sentences.text: Synechodus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes, meaning it was a cartilaginous fish.

Skeletal remains of Synechodus dubrisiensis are known from the Cretaceous of Europe, while a skeleton of an indeterminate species from the Early Cretaceous of France measured around 70 cm in body length.
The genus Synechodus was described by Woodward in 1888.
Synechodus had multicusped teeth used for grasping prey.
Synechodus is known from 16 species that lived primarily from the Late Triassic to the Paleocene, spanning from the Sakmarian to the Lutetian, between 293.52 and 41.03 million years ago.
The oldest known Synecodontiformes from the Early Permian of Russia were assigned to the genus as Synechodus antiquus, though this attribution is debated by other authors.
